_about: Weak points on a hadith's chain. Read by services/usul/rule.py; the build (scripts/build_usul.py) and the endpoint both use it.

levels: Ibn Hajar's twelve ranks of narrators, Taqrib al-Tahdhib preface. terms are his words for each level, plus the data's spelling (صحابي, رمي). Matched whole words, longest term first, on text folded the same way (letters only, one alef, one hamza seat). The level of a narrator is the highest matched, except that under: N marks a level defined as falling short of level N, whose terms count only when no term above N was matched (Ibn Hajar: level 5 is من قصر عن الرابعة قليلا, so a ثقة with رمي stays 3). Words no term takes are listed in usul.db's gap table and never guessed.
kind: what sort of weakness the level is. kinds: a term that is a different sort inside its level (رمي in level 5 is an innovation, the rest of 5 are memory).
weak_from: the lowest level that counts as a weak point. Below it nothing is marked.
max_change_ratio: the build stops if the number of notes moves more than this against the file it would replace, so a broken rule cannot ship quietly.
gap_print: how many of the commonest unmatched wordings the build prints.
levels_source: the sources key the twelve levels come from, printed under each weak point.

lift: the one place a source says support lifts, or does not lift, a weakness. Keyed by level, or by kind where the level has several. A level with no entry has no line. lifts: false is a source saying it is not lifted. book is a key of sources.
sources: where each rule is written. openiti is the text id of the one edition the build reads (books, below, fetches it). Each quote carries its own page.

verify: the build finds every quote that names a book and a page (a dict with quote, book and page, anywhere in this file) in that book's text, and stops where the page it derives, the one a page marker closes (OpenITI marks the END of a page), is not the page written here. elision: inside a quote it splits the quote into parts, each found after the one before it, within gap letters. strip: an editor's folio mark that holds letters ([6 / ظ]), taken out of the book before the quote is looked for.

family: the versions fold of a hadith number (services/usul/family.py, built into usul.db). Places: the narrators at each place of the chains counted from the Companion end, across the narrations one book gives under one number; a place one narrator carries in every narration is marked (alone). Never a name for the number (mashhur, aziz, gharib are about every route a hadith has; one book's narrations of one number are not that). companion_group: the rijal.json generation group of Companions. reasons: why a family is left out, as written in the gap table (family_place for the picture, family_word for the words). The compiler's own teachers named together (حدثنا A وB) stand before the chain and are left out; two names at one place further up (no passing-on word between them) are no single line, so no picture. A telling where rijal places a name after the chain's cut (a second chain, or the chain's end, in the text) has no picture and is not compared. min_words: a telling shorter than this is not set against the others (the books write 'like it'). same_text_min: two tellings are set against each other only when the rarity-weighted share of the shorter one's words found in the other reaches this (a word's weight is ln(tellings / tellings holding it), so common words count little); measured on the 5,540 pairs of the books, the pairs read as different reports under one number sit at 0.14 and below, the paraphrased same report at 0.21 and above. clitics: letters that join the front of a word and are no difference, each with the fewest letters the word must keep (a ب off a four-letter word like بيني takes a root letter; stripped at most clitic_max times). rasm: letters that differ only by their dots, one string per group. dot_min: the shortest word (in letters) whose dot pairs are looked for; three-letter words (ابن and أني) match by dots by chance. sample, sample_seed, sample_gap, sample_text: the families (sample_text: letters of a telling printed where it has no plain chain) the build writes for checking by hand (--sample).

death.bands_say: A year written without its hundreds takes the hundreds of his generation from the preface. Generations 3 and 4 are left out: the third and fourth hold men who died before the 100th year as well as after it (of 42 checked against sunnah.com's years, 12 read as written and 28 take the hundred), so their year is not read.
death.quote: وذكرت وفاة من عرفت سنة وفاته منهم، فإن كان من الأولى والثانية: فهم قبل المائة، وإن كان من الثالثة إلى آخر الثامنة: فهم بعد المائة، وإن كان من التاسعة إلى آخر الطبقات: فهم بعد المائتين، ومن ندر عن ذلك بينته

1.say: Level 1 of 5 in tadlis: he is hardly ever described as doing it.
1.quote: من لم يوصف بذلك الا نادرا كيحيى بن سعيد الانصاري

2.say: Level 2 of 5 in tadlis: the imams put up with it and took his hadith into the Sahih.
2.quote: من احتمل الائمة تدليسه وأخرجوا له في الصحيح لامامته وقلة تدليسه في جنب ما روى كالثوري أو كان لا يدلس الا عن ثقة كإبن عيينة

3.say: Level 3 of 5 in tadlis: the imams took his hadith only where he states hearing.
3.quote: من أكثر من التدليس فلم يحتج الائمة من أحاديثهم الا بما صرحوا فيه بالسماع ومنهم من رد حديثهم مطلقا ومنهم من قبلهم

4.say: Level 4 of 5 in tadlis: agreed that none of his hadith is used unless he states hearing.
4.quote: اتفق على أنه لا يحتج بشئ من حديثهم الا بما صرحوا فيه بالسماع

5.say: Level 5 of 5 in tadlis: weak for another reason, so his hadith is rejected even where he states hearing.
5.quote: من ضعف بأمر آخر سوى التدليس فحديثهم مردود ولو صرحوا بالسماع الا أن يوثق من كان ضعفه يسيرا كابن لهيعة

tadlis.label: Possible tadlis
tadlis.say: This link does not state hearing, and Ibn al-Salah gives it the ruling of a mursal.
tadlis.quote: وأن ما رواه المدلس بلفظ محتمل لم يبين فيه السماع والاتصال، حكمه حكم المرسل وأنواعه

tadlis_unclear.label: Tadlis, unclear
tadlis_unclear.say: This link says anna (that). Scholars differ on whether that counts like an (from).
tadlis_unclear.quote: اختلفوا في قول الراوي: أن فلانا قال كذا وكذا؛ هل هو بمنزلة عن في الحمل على الاتصال إذا ثبت التلاقي بينهما، حتى يتبين فيه الانقطاع؟ ... فروينا عن مالك رضي الله عنه أنه كان يرى عن فلان و أن فلانا سواء. وعن أحمد بن حنبل رضي الله عنه أنهما ليسا سواء

skip.say: In the two Sahihs the scholars take hearing as established from another route, so no note is made there.
skip.quote: وما كان في الصحيحين وشبههما عن المدلسين بعن محمول على ثبوت السماع من جهة أخرى

tellers: عمرو بن عبد الله بن عبيد السبيعي
unless.say: Shu'ba stands below him in this strand: his hadith through Shu'ba shows hearing even when worded عن.
unless.quote: فهذه قاعدة جيدة في أحاديث هؤلاء الثلاثة أنها إذا جاءت من طريق شعبة دلت على السماع ولو كانت معنعنة

tellers: محمد بن مسلم بن تدرس المكي
unless.say: al-Layth stands below him, and what he took from Jabir through al-Layth is what he heard from Jabir.
unless.quote: ونظيره ثنا الليث عن أبي الزبير عن جابر فإنه لم يسمع منه الا مسموعة من جابر

6.en: Accepted when another narrator supports him; otherwise his hadith is soft.
6.quote: مقبول، حيث يتابع، وإلا فلين الحديث

memory.en: A memory fault is lifted when a sound narrator supports him; the hadith becomes good (hasan), though not on its own strength.
memory.quote: ومتى توبع السيء الحفظ بمعتبر ... وكذا المختلط الذي لم يتميز، والمستور، والإسناد المرسل، وكذا المدلس إذا لم يعرف المحذوف منه صار حديثهم حسنا، لا لذاته

7.en: Lifted when a sound narrator supports him; the hadith becomes good (hasan), though not on its own strength.
7.quote: ومتى توبع السيء الحفظ بمعتبر ... وكذا المختلط الذي لم يتميز، والمستور، والإسناد المرسل، وكذا المدلس إذا لم يعرف المحذوف منه صار حديثهم حسنا، لا لذاته

11.en: Support does not lift this weakness.
11.quote: ومن ذلك ضعف لا يزول بنحو ذلك لقوة الضعف ... كالضعف الذي ينشأ من كون الراوي متهما بالكذب

_about: Rulings: what a classical ruling book says of one hadith, quoted and never inferred. Read by services/usul/ruling.py (what a unit says), services/usul/match.py (which of our hadith it is) and scripts/build_usul.py.

shared.strip: the editors' footnote numbers, taken out of every quote. strip also takes the editor's lone 0 between sentences (Ibn Shahin). stop: where a sentence ends; soft_stop (!) ends one only at a paragraph end or before another speaker. speaker_join and title_join: how two scholars' names and a chapter and its title are written together. dangling: a last word no sentence ends on (a relative, conjunction, preposition, colon): a remark ending so runs on into the next unit and is cut back to its last full stop. qualifier: a word that opens the next sentence and takes it back in (إلا, لكن ...), so a quote goes on through it.

kinds: one per book, in the book's own terms. label and say are what the term list prints; quote_label what the sheet calls the quote; asked: keep the question before each answer. ordinal: the grammar of Arabic ordinals, built into `another` where it says {ordinal}. chain_start: the first word of a chain, which ends a bab's title (a روى after ما is part of the title). The other keys are the patterns that cut the ruling out of a unit (see ruling.py).

match: set on scratchpad/usul2-tune.md, hand-labelled pairs kept apart from the sample that was reviewed. df_max: a 3-gram in more of our hadith than this is too common to count. floor: the least summed rarity of shared 3-grams for a match. whole_floor and whole: a short matn may match on this lower score when the hadith holds this share of all the rarity the unit's matn could score. tie_ratio: another hadith within this share of the best score also gets the ruling (the same text in two collections).

match.min_name_words and rare_men: a run of at least this many name words the unit's chain shares with ours is the same man when no more than rare_men narrators carry it, so a common kunya like أبو عبد الرحمن is never enough. rare_name: or one shared name word our chains name in no more than this many places (a Companion named in thousands of chains is no evidence alone). name_run: the longest run of name words compared.

nasikh_chapter.label: In a book of abrogation
nasikh_chapter.say: Ibn Shahin placed this hadith in his book of abrogating and abrogated hadith, under the chapter heading shown. A remark is his, made at this point in the chapter; it may speak of other hadith there.
nasikh_chapter.quote_label: His remark at this point in the chapter

ilal.label: Asked of Abu Hatim or Abu Zur'a
ilal.say: Ibn Abi Hatim asked his father Abu Hatim, or Abu Zur'a, about this hadith. The answer is quoted.
ilal.question: ^\[?(?:(?:أخبرنا|أنا) أبو محمد[^:؛]*[:؛]\s*قال\s*:?\s*)?(?:(?:و|ف)?(?:سألت|سئل)\]?|و?سمعت(?= أبي| أبا))\s*(?P<who>(?:و?(?:أبي|أبا|أبو|زرعة|حاتم)\s*)+)(?!\s*يقول)(?P<lead>(?:\s*(?:و?ذكر|و?سئل|عن|(?:ال)?حديث(?:ا|ين)?|أحاديث|هذا|الذي|رواه(?:ما)?|رواها|رووه)(?![ء-ي]))*)
ilal.author: ^(?:قال أبو محمد|(?:أخبرنا|أنا) أبو محمد)

mawdu_listed.label: Among the fabricated hadith
mawdu_listed.say: Ibn al-Jawzi listed this hadith in his book of fabricated hadith. The sentence quoted judges it, by him or by a critic he cites.
